bluf: NeoMam Studios is a London content marketing studio, founder led by Danny Ashton since 2011 with 13 named team members, selling data led campaigns that earn editorial links, LLM citations and brand authority. It does one thing: original research campaigns, the latest a study quantifying AI slop on YouTube that earned 639 links for a video editing tool client. Where it is going: toward LLM citations as the sold outcome, without an audited product behind them. The thing a rival should know: the Horus read gives it a Tailwind of 40.7, all 15 clients are logos with no described work, and its sitemap shows 1 URL updated in 365 days.
doing:
NeoMam positions itself as a human first content marketing studio making data led, shareable campaigns that earn editorial links, LLM citations and brand authority: content by people, for people. In plain words: a digital PR shop that sells research campaigns for links and now for AI citations, and that markets human authorship as the product. Its headline claim is that a study quantifying AI slop on YouTube earned 639 links for a video editing tool client, quoted as its claim; the client is not named.

The sold mix is one line: content and digital PR, scored 3 on the homepage title branding it a human first content marketing agency and showcased campaigns reporting 104 to 639 earned links. AI search scores 1 with no evidence note, and every other capability scores 0, so breadth is 2. Services: content marketing campaigns, original research, editorial backlinks (digital PR), LLM citations, and authority and thought leadership. No proprietary product and no partner is listed. The prominence signals are editorial rather than commercial: it states it is IPSO regulated and holds content to press editorial standards, holds a creator profile on Visual Capitalist linked from its site schema, and was featured in CoverageBook's Inside Innovation series.

AI posture: it positions against AI content, betting on human made research over low effort AI slop, while pitching LLM citations as a campaign outcome, a stance and a sale at once. Moves: none dated in the record; the status note records recent campaigns and a Sep 2026 sitemap update, with no news, case studies or jobs captured. Pricing signals: a homepage testimonial headed Expensive but worth it implies premium pricing, with no rates published. Conspicuously absent for a digital PR studio of its kind: any measurement of the citations it sells (no audited AI visibility product, no llms.txt on its own site), any SEO line, and any described case for the 15 logos it shows.
clients:
The record types the client base as mixed across automotive, B2B, finance, health, home, media, nonprofit and public interest, retail, technology and travel. The home market is the UK, London headquartered, with no other office listed.

The needs read lists 15 clients, 0 observed and 15 named only, all client logos on the clients page with nothing about the work: Visa, Charles Schwab, AVIS, Compare the Market, MoneySuperMarket, M&S Bank, We Buy Any Car, Adecco, ZenBusiness, Budget Direct, ClickMechanic, Moorepay, Jennings Motor Group, AutoInsurance.com and Sunbelt Staffing, so no mix can be computed; the need is inferred from the single sold line, PR, reputation and content, links first. The one described engagement is unnamed: the video editing tool client behind the AI slop study and its 639 links, a PR and content need observed as a claim. The prominence signal singles out Visa, Charles Schwab, AVIS and Compare the Market as the names the client list spans.

Shared clients: Compare the Market with merkle, MoneySuperMarket with propellernet, Sunbelt Staffing with search-laboratory. The whole book is names only (15 of 15), which the record flags as a question to ask its clients.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places NeoMam best for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ8 (human provenance becomes a distribution signal), both driven by content and digital PR, and most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out). It is likely, with moderate confidence, that these finance and comparison brands will ask for citation share numbers alongside link counts, and a roughly even chance that they accept human authorship as a premium once AI labeling penalties start to bite.

openings:
The strongest opening is the number behind the citation. NeoMam sells LLM citations as a campaign outcome with no audited AI visibility product, no llms.txt and no citation share figure in its record; its proof is link counts (104 to 639). It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival showing a measured citation share for a comparison or finance brand takes the LLM citation budget from Compare the Market or MoneySuperMarket. Falsifier: NeoMam publishing a citation scorecard or tracking product for a named client.

Second, the shoppers: Compare the Market with merkle, MoneySuperMarket with propellernet and Sunbelt Staffing with search-laboratory are each a roughly even chance to be contested on the content line. Third, pricing: the record's only signal is a testimonial headed Expensive but worth it and no rates, so an outcome priced link and citation offer is a conversation it cannot hold in public, and the Monsoon displacement of 57.2 (inferred) says the book is price aware. Fourth, KJ6: a one line studio of 13 people is exposed to the hollowing, though its human provenance stance is the hedge KJ8 rewards. Fifth, the idle house: 1 URL updated in 365 days on a site that sells publishing.
watch: I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, next reading 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas would reward the human first stance and strengthen KJ8, its second tailwind.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: search and other growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the link value it sells, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and KJ1, its first tailwind.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk behind KJ1.

I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: outcome pricing at a top five holdco sets a reference against a studio whose only price signal is Expensive but worth it.

No dated move sits in the record; the follow up is whether the AI slop study campaign is joined by a citation number, which would close the gap between the LLM citations it sells and the links it proves.
